---
title: "Retraction Analysis Library"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
---

Descriptive analysis of retraction watch data, downloaded [here](https://www.crossref.org/labs/retraction-watch/).

Now located [here](https://gitlab.com/crossref/retraction-watch-data). SJR Data located [here](https://github.com/Michael-E-Rose/SCImagoJournalRankIndicators).

Explanation for the categories is [here](https://retractionwatch.com/retraction-watch-database-user-guide/retraction-watch-database-user-guide-appendix-b-reasons/)

The evidence that "withdrawal" used to be a term is [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20240520103212/https://retractionwatch.com/retraction-watch-database-user-guide/retraction-watch-database-user-guide-appendix-b-reasons/). Still present at last crawl of 2024, and absent by the [first crawl of 2025](https://web.archive.org/web/20250124120100/https://retractionwatch.com/retraction-watch-database-user-guide/retraction-watch-database-user-guide-appendix-b-reasons/).

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Install the local library with: devtools::install("retractionwatch")
# or load it during development with: devtools::load_all("retractionwatch")
# At the moment we are using the development version
devtools::install("retractionwatch")
devtools::load_all("retractionwatch")
# Once the package is installed, you can load it with library(retractionwatch)
# library(retractionwatch)
library(plotly)

source("checkpoints.R")
checkpoint_version <- "library"

# # Loading data

sjr_country_counts <- build_sjr_country_counts("data/sjr_rankings")
oecd_countries <- load_oecd_countries("data/oecd_countries.csv")
retraction_data <- load_retraction_data("data/retraction_watch.csv")
publication_counts <- publication_counts_by_class(sjr_country_counts, oecd_countries)
retraction_data_nomass <- retraction_data[retraction_data$Mass_Retraction == "Other",]

checkpoint(retraction_data, "01_retraction_data")
checkpoint(sjr_country_counts, "02_sjr_country_counts")
checkpoint(publication_counts, "03_publication_counts")
```

# New analysis: between country explanation for rates

We know that changes over time in both a) how retractions are reported, and b)
retraction watch's data processing practice for them make temporal patterns
complex to interpret. What is more robust is inter-country comparisons.

```{r}
print("Debuging checks")
print(summary(retraction_data))
```

```{r}
retraction_rates <- compute_retraction_rates(retraction_data, publication_counts)
checkpoint(retraction_rates, "04_retraction_rates")
autorange_axes(ggplotly(plot_retraction_rates(retraction_rates)))
```

# Applying reasons: United Kingdom vs Other OECD

Statistical comparison of the retraction reasons between the UK and the rest of the OECD **excluding the mass retractions**. The for each period (pre and post 2017) and retraction reason, computes the proportion and count of retractions in the UK and the rest of the OECD, the difference in proportions, a two-sample proportion test p-value and its Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.

```{r}
reasons_compare_results <- retraction_data_nomass |>
  reason_flags("country_class") |>
  compare_reason_groups(group_col = "country_class", group_a = "United Kingdom", group_b = "Other OECD")
ratios <- group_count_ratios(reasons_compare_results, "United Kingdom", "Other OECD")
reasons_compare_results <- flag_low_counts(reasons_compare_results, ratios)

checkpoint(reasons_compare_results, "05_reasons_compare_results")

ggplotly(plot_reason_counts_scatter(reasons_compare_results, ratios))
```

```{r}
print("Reason flags ")
print(reason_flags(retraction_data, "country_class"))
print(reasons_compare_results)
```

```{r}
sig_plot <- significant_reasons_long(reasons_compare_results,
                                     p_col = "p_adj_filtered",
                                     exclude_low_count = TRUE)
plot_significant_reasons(sig_plot)

print(sig_plot %>% filter(period == "Post-2017"))
```

```{r}
ggplotly_free_space(plot_significant_reasons(sig_plot))
```

# Retraction reasons of significant adequate counts

```{r}
alpha <- 0.05
low_count <- 500

filtered_reasons <- reasons_compare_results %>%
  filter(p_adj_filtered < alpha & !low_count, period == "Post-2017")

print(filtered_reasons$flag)
```

```{r}

```

The mean proportions for the significant and with adequate count reasons across the years 2017 and 2026, and the interquartile range for the UK and the rest of the OECD. Excluding mass retractions.

```{r}
ggplotly(plot_reason_proportions_forest(
  retraction_data_uk %>% filter(Mass_Retraction == "Other"),
  retraction_data_oecd %>% filter(Mass_Retraction == "Other"),
  reasons_list = selected_reasons,
  labels = c("UK", "Other OECD"),
  year_limits = c(2017, 2026)), height = 300)
```

# Top 10 OECD countries (without the UK) by number of retractions since 2017

Excluding mass retractions

```{r}
# A paper with authors in several countries counts once for each of them
top_10_oecd_countries <- retraction_data_nomass |>
  filter(retraction_year >= 2017) |>
  filter(Country %in% oecd_countries$Name) |>
  distinct(`Record ID`, Country) |>
  count(Country, name = "retractions", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

print(top_10_oecd_countries)
```

```{r}
top_10_oecd_countries
```

```{r}
significant_reasons_per_country_and_year <- calculate_proportion_of_retractions_per_year(
  retraction_data_nomass,
  country_list = top_10_oecd_countries,
  reasons = selected_reasons,
  yearmin = 2017,
  yearmax = 2026)
```

```{r}
plots <- lapply(unique(significant_reasons_per_country_and_year$Reason), function(reason) {
ggplotly(ggplot(significant_reasons_per_country_and_year |> filter(Reason == reason),
       aes(x = year, y = proportion, colour = Country)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = reason,
       x = "Year",
       y = "Proportion of retractions",
       colour = "Country") +
  theme_minimal()
)})
htmltools::tagList(plots)
```

```{r}
plots <- lapply(unique(significant_reasons_per_country_and_year$Reason), function(reason) {
  ggplotly(ggplot(significant_reasons_per_country_and_year |> filter(Reason == reason),
       aes(x = factor(year), y = factor(Country, levels = rev(top_10_oecd_countries$Country)),
           fill = proportion)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 1),
              colour = ifelse(proportion > mean(range(proportion)), "white", "black")),
          size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent, option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  labs(title = reason,
       x = "Year",
       y = "Country",
       fill = "Proportion of\nretractions") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
  )})
htmltools::tagList(plots)
```

Average proportion of retractions citing each reason across the top 10 countries. The shaded bands show the interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile) across the top countries. Each country counts the same, whatever its number of retractions, and countries without retractions in a year are left out of that year.

```{r}
plot_reason_proportions_across_groups_by_year(significant_reasons_per_country_and_year,
                                      interactive = TRUE)
```
